queries.name: firewall-domain-totals
queries.subject: Show each observed firewall domain with the number of runs and total accepted and blocked requests.
queries.objective: Identify domains with observed denied requests for a closer review of firewall evidence.
queries.acceptance: Report distinct observed runs and native accepted and blocked request totals by domain; a denied request alone does not justify allowing egress, and no row does not prove no requests occurred.
queries.description: Distinct runs and accepted and blocked request totals by firewall domain.

queries.name: firewall-most-blocked-domains
queries.subject: Highlight the domains with the most blocked firewall requests.
queries.objective: Prioritize up to ten observed domains by blocked request total for investigation.
queries.acceptance: Rank by observed blocked totals and inspect underlying domain/workflow evidence before deciding whether a block needs attention; the ranking is not a policy authorization or an incidence rate.
queries.description: The ten domains with the highest observed blocked request totals.

queries.name: firewall-domain-workflows
queries.subject: Show workflows that allowed or blocked requests to each observed firewall domain.
queries.objective: Locate which observed workflows contributed accepted or denied requests for a domain.
queries.acceptance: Preserve workflow scope, source link, distinct runs, and native accepted and blocked totals; investigate the run and egress context rather than assuming a denied request is a failure or grounds for wider access.
queries.description: Workflow-level accepted and blocked request totals by firewall domain.

queries.name: mcp-tool-totals
queries.subject: Group observed MCP activity by tool and count calls and calling workflows, excluding the internal safe outputs server.
queries.objective: Expose tool-level call, workflow, and byte totals to investigate observed MCP usage.
queries.acceptance: Group only observed non-safe-output-server calls by server and tool, preserving counts and byte totals; lack of calls does not establish no access, and call volume does not establish value or permission.
queries.description: Observed MCP tool-call totals grouped by MCP server and tool, with the number of distinct calling workflows.

queries.name: mcp-top-tools
queries.subject: Show the ten most frequently called MCP tools.
queries.objective: Identify up to ten tools with the highest observed non-safe-output-server call counts for inspection.
queries.acceptance: Rank observed calls by tool label and inspect grouped tool evidence before drawing conclusions; do not treat popularity as effectiveness or authority to add tools.
queries.description: The ten MCP tools with the most observed calls, excluding the internal safe outputs server.

queries.name: steering-events
queries.subject: Prepare observed gateway steering warnings for aggregation by steering type and workflow.
queries.objective: Expose warning identity, run context, type, and timestamp for downstream steering diagnostics.
queries.acceptance: Project recorded gateway steering events with workflow and run attribution where available; a warning is not a completed budget overrun, failure, or reason to increase limits.
queries.description: Gateway steering warnings emitted when a run approaches its AI Credit budget, time limit, or another declared limit, labelled with a readable steering type.

queries.name: steering-type-totals
queries.subject: Show how often each kind of steering warning occurred.
queries.objective: Identify steering warning categories to inspect in their run context.
queries.acceptance: Report observed event totals and distinct runs and workflows by type; confirm underlying warnings before interpreting frequency, and do not infer actual limit breaches.
queries.description: Observed gateway steering warnings grouped by steering type with the number of affected runs and workflows.

queries.name: steering-workflow-totals
queries.subject: Count steering warnings for each workflow.
queries.objective: Expose workflow-level warning totals and token/time warning breakdowns for downstream review.
queries.acceptance: Count recorded events and distinct runs by workflow, retaining the declared token/time categories; other types remain in total events and no warning alone establishes a failure.
queries.description: Gateway steering warnings grouped by workflow, split into token-budget and time-limit warnings.

queries.name: steering-workflows
queries.subject: Present workflow steering totals with a link to each workflow dashboard.
queries.objective: Show observed workflow steering totals with navigation to the affected run context.
queries.acceptance: Keep workflow identity, link, events, runs, and warning breakdowns tied to their grouped evidence; use drill-through before recommending changes, not warning counts as a basis to widen budgets.
queries.description: Workflow steering totals labelled with a link to the workflow runtime page.

queries.name: steering-top-workflows
queries.subject: Highlight the workflows with the most steering warnings.
queries.objective: Prioritize up to ten workflows by observed warning count for investigation.
queries.acceptance: Rank recorded warning totals with workflow context, checking underlying events and telemetry coverage; a high rank neither proves overrun nor justifies a limit change.
queries.description: The ten workflows with the highest observed gateway steering warning totals.

views.title: Workflows
views.description: Workflows that allowed or blocked requests to the selected firewall domain.
views.empty-message: No workflows allowed or blocked requests to this domain.

pages.intent: Determine which recurring steering warning needs a CAO limit investigation.
pages.subject: Retained gateway steering observations in the selected scope and horizon.
pages.objective: Prioritize investigation of repeated warnings without assuming their cause.
pages.acceptance: Group by native warning type and workflow; expose counts and drill-down evidence. Warnings are observations, not proof of overspend or failed outcomes; retain missing-data states.
pages.title: Steering
pages.description: Identify workflows whose retained steering warnings require a CAO limit investigation.

views.title: Steering types
views.subject: Compare observed steering warnings by type.
views.objective: Choose which warning categories to investigate first.
views.acceptance: A warning category is investigated using its underlying events; no warning is mistaken for a completed failure.
views.description: The share of observed steering warnings by steering type, such as running out of tokens or running out of time.
views.empty-message: No steering warnings were observed in the selected horizon.

views.title: Workflows with the most steering
views.subject: Rank workflows by observed steering warnings.
views.objective: Find workflows that may need a closer look at their run evidence.
views.acceptance: Priority is based on observed counts, with no claim that unlisted workflows had no warnings.
views.description: The ten workflows with the highest observed steering warning totals.
views.empty-message: No workflow steering warnings were observed in the selected horizon.

views.title: Workflows with steering entries
views.description: Observed steering warnings by workflow, split into token-budget and time-limit warnings.
views.empty-message: No workflow steering warnings were observed in the selected horizon.

pages.intent: Determine which blocked egress domain needs workflow-level investigation.
pages.subject: Observed domain request counts in the selected scope and horizon.
pages.objective: Investigate necessary versus unexpected egress without weakening controls by default.
pages.acceptance: Keep accepted and blocked counts distinct; rank blocked domains and retain domain-to-workflow drill-downs. Missing telemetry is not zero blocks or permission to allow a domain.
pages.title: Firewall
pages.description: Identify blocked egress domains that require a workflow-level CAO investigation.

views.title: Most blocked domains
views.description: The ten domains with the highest observed blocked request totals.
views.subject: Prioritize investigation of the most blocked domains and workflows; blocked traffic alone does not justify access.
views.objective: Refresh firewall evidence; query firewall-domain-workflows with --param domain=DOMAIN. Confirm blocked traffic is needed before proposing egress changes.
views.acceptance: Record domain/workflow, time, blocked/allowed counts and disposition (expected denial, unnecessary traffic, justified access). Without fresh evidence, report investigation as incomplete, not zero. Review justified changes with a new snapshot.
views.empty-message: No blocked firewall domains are available for this selection.

views.title: Domains
views.description: Observed runs and accepted and blocked requests by normalized domain.
views.empty-message: No observed firewall domains are available for this selection.

pages.intent: Determine which workflows account for requests to the selected firewall domain.
pages.subject: Retained domain observations matching the domain route parameter.
pages.objective: Locate source workflows and runs for a bounded egress investigation.
pages.acceptance: Preserve the exact domain, repository/workflow identity and accepted/blocked counts; link evidence and disclose partial or unavailable coverage. Do not infer authorization from requests.
pages.title: Workflows
pages.description: Trace the selected firewall domain's decisions to their source workflows.

pages.intent: Determine which MCP tool failure needs workflow-level investigation.
pages.subject: Retained MCP tool invocations in the selected scope and horizon.
pages.objective: Prioritize tool-reliability investigation using observed execution evidence.
pages.acceptance: Show tool identity, invocation and failure counts, workflow context and available provenance. Keep absent telemetry distinct from no failures; do not infer root cause from counts.
pages.title: MCP activity
pages.description: Identify MCP tools whose observed failures require a workflow-level reliability investigation.

views.title: Top MCP tools
views.subject: Compare observed MCP tool call counts, excluding the internal safe outputs server.
views.objective: Identify frequently used tools for further usage review.
views.acceptance: The ranking is interpreted as observed usage only, not tool effectiveness or permission authority.
views.description: The ten most frequently called MCP tools, excluding the internal safe outputs server.
views.empty-message: No MCP tool activity was observed.

views.title: MCP tools
views.description: Observed MCP activity grouped by tool, excluding the internal safe outputs server.
views.empty-message: No MCP tool activity was observed.
